paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: wisdom is better than strength (Ecclesiastes 9:16). The Teacher's proof is a poor wise man who saved a small city that a mighty king came against (Ecclesiastes 9:14-15). It was his wisdom that saved the city, not anybody's strength. Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but the Teacher also says one sinner destroys much good (Ecclesiastes 9:18).

So how do you live that out? Slow down, baker, and get skilled instead of just working harder. The Teacher says, "If the axe is dull and the blade unsharpened, more strength must be exerted, but skill produces success" (Ecclesiastes 10:10). He also says the calm words of the wise are heeded over the shouts of a ruler among fools (Ecclesiastes 9:17), and I say that as the LOUDEST stamper in the Dorinverse. Gracious words and steady hands are the wiser way, even when noise gets the attention, and tiny folly can spoil a lot, like dead flies in the perfumer's oil (Ecclesiastes 10:1), so guard the little things.

Here's the part that matters most: wisdom doesn't always get a parade, and that's okay. Your good choices might go unnoticed, just like that poor man's. But the Teacher called that wisdom great (Ecclesiastes 9:13), and it still saved the city. So keep sharpening the axe, baker, keep your words gracious, and keep showing up at your post, whether anybody claps or not.
